title: Memory access simulation
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query indices and each finite Boolean word, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. Choose a site $st$, a machine state $S$, and a memory $M\colon\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Assume every counter of $S$ is at most $B$, its outward-walk, return-walk, and scratch counters are zero, and the address $a$ given by the memory-region base plus the counter selected by $st$ is at most both $B$ and $P$. Starting in the access routine for $st$ with state $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$, the machine reaches the exit specified by $st$ and the bit $st.set\lor M(a)$, with state again $S$, head again at $0$, and memory changed only by setting cell $a$ to true when $st$ is a marking site. At every earlier configuration, all counters are at most $B$, the memory head lies between $0$ and $P$, register comparisons use distinct registers, input comparisons are made only on inputs with the required valid plain or paired form, and oracle calls use lists of distinct registers.

Every counter of $S$ is at most $B$
The outward-walk, return-walk, and scratch counters of $S$ are zero

replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of
four query types and each finite bit string, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let
$M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory. Choose a site $st$ from
the initial marking, relaxation-round reads or marking, count read, or final-scan read;
it selects either the $U$ or $V$ counter, and is a marking site precisely for the
initial marking and the relaxation-round marking. Let $S$ be a machine state whose 17
natural-number counters are all at most $B$, with its outward-walk, return-walk, and
scratch counters equal to zero, and suppose the memory address $a$, obtained by adding
the memory-region base in $S$ to the counter selected by $st$, satisfies $a\le B$ and
$a\le P$. Starting in the access routine for $st$, with state $S$, memory $M$, and
memory head at $0$, the machine reaches the exit determined by $st$ and the Boolean
value $st.set\lor M(a)$; the final state is again $S$, the head is at $0$, and the final
memory is $M$ with cell $a$ set to true if $st$ is a marking site, and is $M$ otherwise.
At every earlier configuration in this run, all counters are at most $B$, the memory
head lies between $0$ and $P$, and the program's instruction-specific guard conditions
hold.
